speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these episodes of dizziness and vertigo, and do you feel any specific symptoms like hearing loss or tinnitus during them?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your vertigo is position-dependent and you have a history of presbycusis, I want to rule out Meniere's disease or vestibular schwannoma. Do you notice any hearing fluctuations, ear fullness, or ringing in your ears specifically when the spinning starts? Also, do you experience any nausea, vomiting, or imbalance when standing up quickly?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
